To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tfb2 transcription factor is induced at the mRNA level in response to heat stress, and that a T‐rich terminator sequence in the tfb2 mRNA 5′ leader is responsible for the downregulation of tfb2 gene expression under non‐heat shock conditions.

the tfb2 transcription initiation factor gene in the archaeon H. volcanii is heat shock inducible and that the heat shock‐inducible expression of this gene is regulated in part by a sequence‐dependent termination element in the tfb2 5′‐UTR.

a TFB‐encoding gene in Hfx. volcanii is heat shock inducible at both the transcriptional and translational levels, but that expression of the gene is downregulated at the post‐transcriptional level by a sequence‐dependent termination mechanism that involves a T‐rich element in the DNA leader region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of a heat‐induced archaeal transcription factor and the regulatory mechanisms involved in the heat‐induced expression of this factor.

the characterization of a TFIID‐related transcription factor, TFB2, which is involved in transcription initiation of archaeal genes and which may be involved in the regulation of gene expression during heat stress.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tfb2 transcription initiation gene from H. volcanii is heat responsive and that this regulation is mediated by both a TATA box and a transcription terminator.
the TFB2 gene is induced at the transcriptional level in response to heat stress in H. volcanii.
the TFB2 gene of H. volcanii is regulated at the transcription level in response to heat stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tfb2 transcription unit contains a TATA‐dependent core promoter, a transcription terminator element and a heat‐responsive promoter element.
the tfb2 transcription initiation region contains both positive and negative regulatory elements that control the basal and heat‐induced expression of this gene in H. volcanii.

the tfb2 transcription unit is a heat shock‐inducible gene, which contains a TATA‐containing promoter and a T‐rich element in the 5′‐leader region that functions as a sequence‐specific transcription terminator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the archaeon H. volcanii possesses a TFIIB gene, and that this gene has a heat shock‐inducible promoter.
the archaeon H. volcanii has a TATA‐dependent heat‐responsive transcription initiation mechanism that appears to have diverged from the TATA‐independent mechanism found in other archaea.
the tfb2 transcription factor is heat inducible and is regulated by both a promoter‐associated TATA element and a transcription terminator‐associated T‐rich element.
